name: Mustafa Al Shaar
goal: Deliver a secure, persisted inventory API. You own schema changes and shared backend security; other members implement their own modules against your stable foundations.
interfaces: POST /auth/login; GET /auth/me
GET/POST /pharmacist/medicines; PATCH /pharmacist/medicines/:id
POST /pharmacist/medicines/:id/batches; PATCH /pharmacist/batches/:id
Reuse Mohammad's pure inventory calculations and Shiam's effective subscription helper.
week1: Day 1

Run the empty NestJS foundation. Design the Prisma models/relations with the team and agree JWT claims, Actor/guard interfaces and calculation helper signatures. You author the database, migrations, Prisma service and demo seed; none are prebuilt.
Day 2

Implement the initial schema/migration and Prisma service, then build login DTO, bcrypt comparison, JWT issuance and /auth/me. Start a small auth PR; keep schema and guard interfaces stable for teammates.
Day 3

Implement and test JWT, role, ownership and active-subscription write guards plus the business-date utility. Share the imports/interfaces with Shiam and Hamid. Begin seed data; finish it alongside inventory work.
Day 4
Implement medicine create/update/list with trim+case uniqueness, own-pharmacy scoping, query DTOs and database conflict mapping. Use Mohammad's calculation helper for response indicators.
Day 5
Implement batch creation and edit. Allow already expired stock; reject invalid quantity/date/cost. Only quantity, expiry and location are editable. Keep immutable batch fields rejected in PATCH DTO.
Day 6
Wrap medicine/batch mutation and inventoryUpdatedAt in one transaction. Complete name/status filtering, count and multiple indicators; add Swagger response DTOs and meaningful logs.
Day 7
Buffer/review: run API tests, seed and migrate on a clean dedicated database. Merge a usable inventory API by the end of Week 1; record any blockers in the team plan.
week2: Day 8
Integrate real inventory/sign-in requests with Alaa. Compare API payloads with shared contracts; fix backend mismatches rather than adding mock fallback.
Day 9
Add regression tests: guessed cross-pharmacy medicine/batch IDs, owner inventory attempt, missing/wrong token, inactive subscription read versus write.
Day 10
Verify duplicate names across pharmacies, duplicate batches, unknown fields, fractional quantities, negative cost and invalid dates. Failed writes must leave inventoryUpdatedAt unchanged.
Day 11
Exercise every inventory indicator filter with Mohammad's fixtures. Verify calendar boundaries and decimal serialization; preserve simultaneous indicators.
Day 12
Review the other backend modules for guard coverage and ownership/privacy errors with their owners. Check persisted data survives restart and migrations apply on another laptop.
Day 13
Run owner->pharmacist->public flow with team. Freeze schema and API shapes; fix only core defects. Review seed coverage and prepare Swagger examples.
Day 14
Buffer/final rehearsal: show login, a forbidden guessed-ID request and database persistence. Explain controller->service->Prisma and why medicine differs from batch in English.
checks: A01/A02: missing/invalid token and wrong role fail; owner cannot edit inventory; cross-pharmacy read/write fails.
A05: inactive pharmacists read but cannot change medicines/batches; clear 403 reason.
A07/A08: normalized duplicate names/batches conflict; bad dates/negative or fractional quantities/immutable PATCH fields rejected.
A10/A12: filters include every relevant indicator; stock mutation and timestamp are atomic.
A17: clean migrations, repeatable seed, restart persistence and Swagger match contracts.
handoffs: Day 1: agree Actor/JWT/guard imports and schema fields. You author these; none is prebuilt.
Day 2-3: auth/guard PR available for all backend owners.
Day 2: receive calculation helper from Mohammad; write service tests with fixed sample inputs while waiting.
Day 6-7: inventory endpoints ready for Alaa. Day 8 begins API integration.
presentation: Show authenticated Swagger inventory access, reject an unauthorized/cross-pharmacy write, then show the persisted PostgreSQL record. Explain one transaction and one uniqueness rule.
avoid: Do not take over owner/duty/dashboard services or frontend pages. Review colleagues' PRs instead. Do not add optional dispensing, sales, AI or deployment.

name: Shiam Ezzo
goal: Build one focused owner module: pharmacies, pharmacist accounts and subscription management. Build your owner module and subscription helper yourself. Agree the schema and authentication interfaces with Mustafa; authentication is his separate responsibility.
interfaces: GET/POST /owner/pharmacies; POST /owner/pharmacists
POST/PATCH/DELETE /owner/pharmacies/:id/subscription
Implement/test effectiveSubscriptionStatus(subscription,today); agree this reusable interface with other API owners.
All routes OWNER-only; return OwnerPharmacy/Subscription/SessionUser shapes from contracts.
week1: Day 1

Run the empty backend. Agree Pharmacy/User/Subscription fields with Mustafa, then plan your own owner controller/service/DTOs and subscription-status helper. Read the exact status rules in the teacher specification.
Day 2

Write effectiveSubscriptionStatus and its tests from scratch: null, future start, inclusive boundaries, expired and suspended. Share its interface/PR early. Use your own fake Prisma fixtures while authentication is in progress.
Day 3
Implement create pharmacy and list/search pharmacies. Return effective subscription status using one captured business date; add DTO validation and explicit response mapping.
Day 4
Implement pharmacist account creation linked to an existing pharmacy. Normalize email, hash initial password, reject duplicates and never return/log the hash.
Day 5
Implement create subscription: one per pharmacy, strict date validation, end after start. Test conflict for a second subscription; use the database unique constraint.
Day 6
Implement subscription date edits, suspend/reactivate and deletion. Delete only Subscription; all stock/accounts/duty/history must remain. Log safe business events.
Day 7
Buffer/review: attach Mustafa's guards, add owner-only Swagger docs and status filters. Open a complete owner API PR for Week 1 review.
week2: Day 8
Connect the real owner endpoints with Alaa's UI. Verify all dates, statuses and validation messages match the contracts.
Day 9
Add controller/API tests: anonymous fails 401, pharmacist fails 403, nonexistent pharmacy/subscription fails 404 and invalid UUID/body fails 400.
Day 10
Run the subscription lifecycle: create ACTIVE, suspend, reactivate, expire through test clock, delete to NONE. Ensure filtering/search uses effective rather than stored status.
Day 11
Pair briefly with Hamid and Mustafa: changing/deleting subscription must remove public listing and block pharmacist writes while preserving reads/data.
Day 12
Check dates in Asia/Amman around midnight; add regression tests for future-start NONE and suspended-but-expired precedence. Fix Swagger/example/error inconsistencies.
Day 13
Full-flow rehearsal with seeded owner and two pharmacist accounts. Confirm no password/hash in any owner response. Prepare English demo steps.
Day 14
Buffer/final fixes. Show owner onboarding and subscription deletion preserving pharmacy data. Explain ACTIVE/EXPIRED/SUSPENDED/NONE in English.
checks: A03: owner creates pharmacy and pharmacist linked to it; email conflict/nonexistent pharmacy rejected.
A04: inclusive date boundaries, suspension precedence, future/missing NONE; one subscription only; end>start.
A06: deleting subscription retains users/pharmacy/medicines/batches/duty exactly.
A01/A05: only owner changes subscriptions; inactive pharmacist read/write/public behavior integrates correctly.
Unknown fields rejected; proper HTTP errors; summaries/parameters/auth/responses in Swagger; safe logs.
handoffs: Independent start: write/test your status helper and service using your own fake data. Agree database fields and wire types on Day 1.
Day 2-3: use Mustafa's shared guards; ask him for review of account creation/security.
Day 5: give Alaa sample owner payloads; Day 7: owner endpoints available.
Day 11: verify subscription effects with Hamid/Mustafa without editing their modules.
presentation: Create a pharmacy/account, change its subscription, delete that subscription and show that inventory still exists. Explain the difference between stored suspension and calculated effective status.
avoid: No frontend, login implementation, inventory edits, billing or schema migrations. Request schema changes from Mustafa. The existing Git branch is spelled Sheam even though the task guide uses Shiam.

name: Hamid Al Haj
role: Profile, duty and public backend; small display-preferences task
goal: Deliver the pharmacy profile/duty APIs and privacy-safe public search/directory. Spend most effort on backend core; language and theme controls are a small follow-up after your core endpoints work.
interfaces: GET/PATCH /pharmacist/profile; GET/POST /pharmacist/duty-periods
PATCH/DELETE /pharmacist/duty-periods/:id
GET /public/medicines?q=&area=&onDutyNow=; GET /public/pharmacies
Implement the PublicPharmacy allowlist; use shared auth/status helpers after their owners merge them. Agree interfaces on Day 1.
week1: Day 1

Agree profile/duty/public response fields and schema needs with the team. Create your own DTOs, service fixtures, public response mapper and fixed-clock tests; no helpers, adapters or dataset are supplied.
Day 2
Implement own profile read/update with area/address/phone validation. Inactive subscription can read; updates require ACTIVE. Do not allow changing pharmacyId or pharmacy name here.
Day 3
Implement duty list/create/edit/delete. Validate offset-aware instants, end>start and duration<=24h; derive pharmacy from actor and enforce guessed-ID ownership.
Day 4
Prevent overlaps, including concurrent requests (serializable transaction/retry or per-pharmacy lock). Exclude the same period on edit; allow adjacent periods. Test overnight and exact start/end.
Day 5
Implement public pharmacy directory: ACTIVE only, area/duty filters, current and next period. Map exact public fields and nested start/end only.
Day 6

Implement medicine search: partial display/scientific name, active subscription and at least one positive nonexpired batch. Combine area/duty filters; deduplicate pharmacies and return empty list normally.
Day 7
Buffer/review: test privacy allowlist and inactive/expired-only/zero-only stock. Document endpoints/DTOs/auth in Swagger; publish profile/duty/public PRs.
week2: Day 8
Integrate profile/duty API with Mohammad and public API with Yousef. Compare payloads; show them current/next/null period examples and proper errors.
Day 9
Add regression cases: subscription delete removes listing, future subscription hidden, exact duty end excluded, different pharmacy overlaps allowed and no private fields leak.
Day 10
Verify all CORE endpoints pass before preferences. Add working persistent light/dark control using theme.css tokens. Keep structural page CSS owned by Alaa.
Day 11

Add EN/AR control and small translation provider/dictionaries. Set document lang and direction; keep medicine/scientific names, phone and batch identifiers readable LTR. Arabic is optional instructor scope: cut translation expansion if core is blocked.
Day 12

With Alaa, connect Preferences in the shell coordinated with Alaa and translate shared labels in one small integration PR. Check dark contrast, keyboard use, persistence and RTL in public/profile pages.
Day 13
Run public availability and overnight-duty rehearsal with the team. Inspect actual JSON for private fields, including nested objects; prepare Swagger privacy example.
Day 14
Buffer/final fixes. Explain overnight intervals, public privacy and eligible stock in English. Show one rejected overlap and a public search result.
checks: A02/A05: own pharmacy only; inactive profile/duty writes forbidden with reason; reads allowed.
A13: overnight, inclusive start/exclusive end, adjacent intervals, >24h, edit-self and simultaneous overlaps.
A14: name/area/duty combine; inactive or expired/zero-only stock never appears; no duplicate pharmacy results.
A15: exact public allowlist and ACTIVE directory; current/next/null periods; no account/subscription/cost/quantity/storage/IDs.
Preferences: persisted light/dark and EN/AR controls, sensible contrast/RTL; do not delay core for optional translation.
handoffs: Independent start: agree schema/response fields and create your own Prisma/clock test fixtures. Use the specification as the source of rules.
Day 2-3: use Mustafa's guards and Shiam's status helper when merged; do not implement another auth/status system.
Day 5: profile/duty examples for Mohammad; Day 6-7: public examples/endpoints for Yousef.
Day 10-12: preferences integration with Alaa only after backend core is stable.
presentation: Show an overnight duty period, reject an overlapping period, then search publicly and inspect the response allowlist in Swagger. Explain why exact quantities stay private.
avoid: No public page layout, dashboard UI, inventory endpoints or schema migrations. No maps, hosting, SMS or citizen accounts. Do not spend Week 1 translating the application.

name: Mohammad Kashmar
role: Dashboard and calculations backend (~60%); dashboard/profile/duty UI (~40%)
goal: Own the shared stock calculations and pharmacist dashboard API, then build dashboard and pharmacy profile/duty screens. Agree response types early and create your own small local test fixtures to build screens before Hamid finishes his endpoints.
interfaces: GET /pharmacist/dashboard -> Dashboard
calculateMedicine(batches,threshold,today) and calculateDashboard(medicines,today): agree signatures with Mustafa Day 1.
Dashboard frontend calls your API; profile/duty frontend calls Hamid's endpoints through feature api.ts.
Backend calculates all indicators; no editable status fields and no authoritative frontend calculations.
week1: Day 1

Agree calculation helper input/output with Mustafa and publish the types. Read all indicator/dashboard rules and write a small hand-calculated fixture with expired, healthy, zero and low+expiring stock.
Day 2
Implement/test pure date/quantity/indicator helper in common/inventory-calculations.ts. Deliver this small PR first so Mustafa can use it without waiting for the dashboard.
Day 3
Test yesterday/today/+90/+91 expiry boundaries, available sums, quantity==threshold and simultaneous indicators. HEALTHY ignores empty expired/soon batches, but nonempty ones prevent healthy.
Day 4

Implement dashboard aggregation with Prisma.Decimal: nonexpired units/value, expiring batch count, low-stock medicines, expired batch count and positive expired waste value. Add hand-calculation tests.
Day 5
Implement own-pharmacy dashboard service/controller using shared auth/role/ownership foundations. Inactive subscription reads remain allowed. Add all attention items with multiple indicators.
Day 6
Document/test dashboard in Swagger. Give Mustafa fixed-date response fixtures and compare inventory filters with the same helper. Keep all calculations in backend services/pure functions.
Day 7
Buffer/review: publish your backend PR. Start dashboard cards and profile/duty forms from scratch with your own feature-local sample data; coordinate shared routing/styles with Alaa.
week2: Day 8
Finish backend regression tests: ownership, inactive reads, empty pharmacy, decimal costs and no expired units in available totals. Connect DashboardPage to your real endpoint.
Day 9
Build all required dashboard metrics, pharmacy name, subscription banner and attention list. Show all relevant badges and loading/empty/error states.
Day 10
Build pharmacy profile form with editable area/address/phone only. Show Hamid's backend validation messages and disable changes for inactive subscription while retaining read access.
Day 11
Build duty list/add/edit/delete forms. Convert datetime-local values with explicit local timezone to UTC ISO; show current periods clearly and surface overlap/end/duration errors.
Day 12

Integrate Hamid's real profile/duty APIs. Refresh views after mutations; check delete confirmation, successful form reset and retained values after errors. Coordinate dashboard refresh after Alaa's inventory changes.
Day 13
Use real API integration for all your screens. Reconcile hand-calculated totals with persisted stock and fix discrepancies with Mustafa. Rehearse keyboard/mobile/error cases.
Day 14
Buffer/final rehearsal. Explain one calculation in English, show multi-indicator attention and an invalid duty change. Know how your shared helper is used by inventory too.
checks: A09: expiry boundaries and calendar days correct; no editable status data.
A10: LOW_STOCK at equality, multiple indicators retained and correct healthy/nonempty handling.
A11: 10x2.50 nonexpired +3x4.00 expired yields value 25.00/waste 12.00/units 10.
Dashboard scoped to own pharmacy and available to inactive subscribers; empty data has honest zero/empty values.
A16: all 3 frontend areas handle loading/empty/error, validation and inactive read-only state; profile/duty mutations refresh.
handoffs: Critical: Day 1 signatures and Day 2 helper PR for Mustafa; this is the main backend dependency.
Independent UI work: create local dashboard/profile/duty fixtures from agreed response types while Hamid builds his endpoints.
Day 7: dashboard API available. Day 8: get Hamid's profile/duty endpoint examples.
Day 12: coordinate a refresh mechanism with Alaa; avoid editing each other's pages directly.
presentation: Explain a dashboard total from actual batches, show a medicine with two indicators and demonstrate a duty/profile edit. Describe why expired stock still contributes to waste but not availability.
avoid: Do not implement inventory mutations, authentication, owner services or public search. Do not store calculated statuses or recompute authoritative totals in React.

name: Yousef Yousef
role: Public medicine search and pharmacy directory frontend
goal: Build two clear public screens from scratch, with simple components and agreed API shapes. No backend, database, sign-in or private inventory work is assigned to you.
interfaces: Create searchMedicines({q,area,onDutyNow}) using response fields agreed with Hamid; no request adapter is provided.
Create listPublicPharmacies({area,onDutyNow}); public DTOs/types must be agreed and written by the team.
Hamid owns these API endpoints. Read public fields only; cards never show stock counts/costs/batches.
Use simple loading/error/badge components you create; ask Alaa for shared layout changes.
week1: Day 1

Run the plain React foundation. Find your public-search/directory folders. Sketch two simple screens and create your first page/card component yourself. Agree public response fields with Hamid and routes with Alaa.
Day 2
Add a labeled medicine input and Search button to PublicSearchPage. Save the submitted query in component state; avoid sending a request on every keypress.
Day 3
Add area text input and on-duty checkbox. Send q/area/onDutyNow through a search request function you create in your feature. Prevent empty medicine submission and keep entered values visible.
Day 4

Build PharmacyCard yourself: name, area, address, phone link, on-duty badge and current/next duty time. Create a small local fixture file to test cards; format dates and handle missing inventory timestamps clearly.
Day 5

Implement loading, no-results and error states yourself, with a helpful message and Retry button. Exercise each state with your own local fixtures or simulated requests; no shared state component is prebuilt.
Day 6
Add area/on-duty filters to DirectoryPage using listPublicPharmacies. Reuse PharmacyCard. Directory opens without requiring a medicine query or sign-in.
Day 7
Buffer/review: check phone-sized layout and keyboard labels. Open Week 1 UI PR with screenshots for search, directory and empty/error examples.
week2: Day 8
With Hamid, switch to real API integration and test search against seeded data. Use your own local test fixtures for isolated styling; final checks must use real API responses.
Day 9
Verify partial/case-insensitive scientific-name search, an area with no matches and area+on-duty together. Report API mistakes to Hamid instead of calculating stock/status in React.
Day 10
Check request changes do not show stale results. Add a visible result count and clear/reset filters; retry errors without losing the current query.
Day 11
Test directory current/next/null duty examples and missing timestamp. Add accurate labels so 'off duty' does not claim a pharmacy is closed; duty status is all we know.
Day 12
Check accessibility: input labels, keyboard order, buttons, meaningful status text and responsive cards. With Hamid, check your pages in dark mode/Arabic if those optional controls are ready.
Day 13
Follow the citizen demo: search medicine, apply duty filter, inspect address/phone, try a no-match term. Confirm no private details appear anywhere in your cards.
Day 14
Buffer/final rehearsal. Present the citizen search and directory in English, show empty/error behavior and explain what information citizens can and cannot see.
checks: Search requires a nonempty medicine query and sends the correct filters; directory does not require medicine text.
All cards show only allowed public fields; no quantity/cost/barcode/batch/subscription information.
Loading, zero results, backend errors, retry and result count work without reloading the browser.
Current/next duty and null values are clear; on-duty badge does not falsely claim general opening hours.
Real API-mode search, scientific names, combined filters, keyboard and narrow-screen layout tested.
handoffs: Start immediately with your own page sketches/components and small local fixtures. Week 1 frontend work does not need a running backend.
Ask Alaa for shared component/style help; keep changes inside your feature folders.
Day 6-7: get Hamid's public JSON examples; Day 8 integrate real API integration.
Report backend defects with search term, filters and observed result so Hamid can reproduce.
presentation: Demonstrate a medicine search, area and duty filtering, the pharmacy contact card and a no-results state. Explain that public availability does not expose exact quantities.
avoid: No backend, database, accounts, owner pages, maps or medical advice. Do not hard-code live results or hide an API error by silently showing sample data.

name: Alaa Ismaiel
role: Frontend foundations, sign-in, owner/inventory UI and integration
goal: Own the remaining frontend and coordinate the complete local demo. Keep teammates independent through shared components and contracts, and merge small working PRs throughout the two weeks.
folders: apps/web/src/styles.css; root docs/config with teammate review
interfaces: Sign-in uses Mustafa's /auth/login + /auth/me and Role/SessionUser contracts.
Owner UI calls Shiam's owner endpoints; inventory UI calls Mustafa's medicine/batch endpoints.
Use Mohammad's dashboard screen and Hamid's Preferences component through routes coordinated with Alaa; Yousef owns public screens.
You review shared types/schema/route changes; Mustafa alone authors Prisma migrations.
week1: Day 1

Publish the foundation-only starter through a PR. Agree API shapes, schema needs, routing and ownership with the team. Create shared TypeScript wire types together; feature folders are empty and the single page is only a startup check.
Day 2

Create the application routes, navigation, responsive shell and shared styles/components yourself. Begin sign-in/logout, session handling and role-specific route protection; coordinate real JWT requests with Mustafa.
Day 3
Build the owner pharmacy list/search/status filters and create-pharmacy form from scratch. Use response types agreed with Shiam and write your own local fixtures while his API is in progress.
Day 4
Build account creation and subscription forms yourself: dates, suspend/reactivate and delete confirmation. Implement request/error handling; use local test data until Shiam's endpoints are ready.
Day 5
Build inventory search/status filters, visible count, batch detail rows and every indicator badge. Inactive subscription keeps read access but disables mutations with a clear explanation.
Day 6
Build medicine create/edit and batch create/edit forms. Read-only batch number/cost/barcode after creation; editable quantity/expiry/location. After success refresh data without page reload.
Day 7
Buffer/review: merge Week 1 PRs, check each member has visible contributions, and start real owner/inventory API integration. Record remaining blockers and avoid large late merges.
week2: Day 8
Connect sign-in/owner/inventory to the real API. Show 400/401/403/404/409 messages, reset stale session on unauthorized responses and use role-specific navigation.
Day 9
Complete real create/update/delete flows and validation feedback. Verify subscription changes refresh owner views and pharmacist read-only status; do not bypass backend rules with client-only checks.
Day 10
Coordinate inventory/dashboard refresh with Mohammad (navigation reload or shared invalidation). Verify low+expiring badges and counts against real API payloads, including empty inventory.
Day 11
Integrate Hamid's preference controls with minimal shared-file edits. Review Yousef's mobile/keyboard public pages; help with reusable components while preserving his ownership.
Day 12

Run docs/ACCEPTANCE.md with all members in real API integration. Confirm clean startup on another member's laptop and no .env/node_modules committed. Fix frontend defects and assign backend fixes to owners.
Day 13
Freeze feature scope, merge tested fixes and rehearse the full English demo: owner onboarding -> stock -> dashboard -> public search -> rejected action -> persisted database.
Day 14
Buffer/final review. Update README with real setup and known limitations. Prepare short presentation sections for all six people; verify demo data/time and every member's understanding.
checks: A16: all owned screens loading/empty/error, backend validation and subscription reason; successful changes refresh views.
Private routes prompt sign-in and enforce role navigation; real integration has no fake-login or sample fallback.
Inventory supports multiple indicators and visible-item count; immutable batch fields are not submitted in PATCH.
Owner can onboard and edit/delete subscriptions while inventory remains preserved; delete confirmation is explicit.
A17/A18: another laptop can start locally; all CORE scenarios checked; every member contributes and speaks English.
handoffs: Day 1: starter PR first; shared contracts/schema discussion; other members then branch from the baseline.
Day 2-3: receive Mustafa auth/guards; frontend can use mocks until ready.
Day 6-8: receive Shiam owner and Mustafa inventory APIs, Hamid public/profile/duty APIs and Mohammad dashboard.
Daily: short status and small PR review; Days 8 and 12 are integration gates, not the first time anyone merges.
presentation: Introduce the problem and product, show owner/inventory UX and loading/error feedback, then hand off to each member. Explain one UI decision and one honest remaining limitation.
avoid: Do not take over other members' assigned features. No deployment, billing, new stack, big design rewrite or optional challenges before CORE is integrated. Do not merge broken builds just to meet a date.
